title: On-prem edge sandboxing and HW constraints - Quasar Imaging
summary: Initial discovery for an air-gapped, on-prem inference deployment at Quasar Imaging. Main topics: hardware footprint, secure offline update process, latency goals vs cost tradeoffs, and integration with existing PACS and imaging pipeline. Customer leaning toward private deployment with possibility of dedicated reserved capacity later. Agreed to run a short latency/throughput benchmark on-site and to share security docs.
topics: KMS/HSM and key management in offline env
integration with PACS and DICOM pipeline
next_steps: Samira: share Redwood private deployment security pack (SOC2, ISO extracts, KMS integration notes) by 2026-07-02
Priya: propose a lightweight benchmark harness and test plan for on-site validation by 2026-07-07
Quasar: provide a list of exact GPU SKUs and server models available at the site by 2026-07-03
action_items: Samira: send example SOW for private deployment and high-level pricing ranges by 2026-07-02
Priya: prep benchmark script (tf/torch trace + synthetic DICOM payload) and share run instructions
Maya: coordinate with facilities to confirm update window and customs clearance constraints for sealed media
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Samira Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Nathan Liu (Redwood notes), Dr. Evan Low (CTO, Quasar), Maya Ortiz (Head of Ops), Raj Patel (Infra), Lina Gomez (Security)

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm samira from Redwood Inference, i'm the account lead here, quick roundtrip intros?
[00:14] Dr. Evan Low: yeah hi i'm evan, cto at quasar imaging, we do inference on large radiology image sets, mostly 3d ct recon, trying to move more models in-house.
[00:29] Maya: maya here, ops - i'm the one who will be scheduling the hardware windows and sign-offs
[00:36] Raj: raj infra, i'll be the one who actually racks hardware and handles network isolation
[00:42] Priya: priya, i'm the se, i'll dig into the latency/cost bits and the patch/update workflow with you all
[00:51] Samira: awesome, thanks. quick agenda: hw footprint and constraints, air-gapped update flow, security requirements (kms, hsm, audit), and next steps. sound good?
[01:05] Lina: yes, and i'd like to cover data residency and audit logs - SOC 2 bits.

Summary/Context exchange:
[01:20] Raj: our primary constraint, we have a sterilized imaging room, rack space limited to 1U or 2U servers in iso cabinets, so GPUs need to be dual-slot low profile or external chassis. power budget per rack is 4KW. we also have NVMe capacity but limited onboard storage, and usb/physical media go through a customs-like security check.
[01:44] Priya: ok so limited rack space, power constraints, and constrained media transfer windows - got it. do you have specific GPU families in mind, or is that open?
[01:56] Dr. Evan Low: we have some older t4s and a couple of a100s for training, but the sterile room is currently going to be provisioned with H100-ish blades if procurement clears, though it may take 6-8 weeks. in the meantime we may test on smaller 80gb a100 and t4.
[02:18] Samira: helpful. also want to understand the model sizes - are you running 30B-ish weights or smaller vision encoders?
[02:27] Dr. Evan Low: most of our production are 7B-13B multimodal encoders and then a few specialized 30B segmentation models. latency targets are tight - sub 250ms for a single image slice request, end-to-end with preprocessing.

On deployment mode and constraints:
[02:45] Priya: given the sterile/air-gapped constraints it sounds like Private (on-prem) is what you want. two options typically: fully air-gapped private control plane with sealed media updates, or a dedicated-reserved mode that keeps a control channel - which you can't do. do you have policy that forbids any egress?
[03:05] Maya: yes, no outbound to the internet from that room, that's a hard requirement from compliance.
[03:11] Priya: ok so we'll assume hermetic mode, updates via signed bundles you bring in via approved media. we support signed release tarballs and an offline installer + attestation flow.
[03:23] Raj: can you describe attestation? what kind of signatures and key mgmt are you expecting? we use an HSM at our primary datacenter but not in the sterile site.
[03:34] Priya: typically we sign release artifacts with a Redwood private key; for air-gapped we can support signed images that you verify against your local KMS/HSM. there is an offline key wrap flow where you perform unwrap with your HSM and we provide signed metadata; also we can integrate with third-party HSMs if you supply PKI material.
[03:51] Lina: how do we rotate keys and prove chain-of-custody for updates? in audits they ask for the manifest and who signed it.
[03:59] Priya: we keep an auditable manifest with SHA256 digests and signer fingerprints; we can export that as part of the install artifact. rotation: you can rotate keys locally and we'll accept signatures from keys in your trust bundle.

Latency vs batching tradeoffs:
[04:20] Samira: evan mentioned <250ms target - is that 1-slice or full study?
[04:27] Dr. Evan Low: that's per-slice, often we stream many slices; for an entire study we can accept longer.
[04:33] Priya: so we need to optimize for single-request latency. that tends to push toward small batch sizes and preferring fp16 or int8 quantized models with optimized kernels. with 7b-13b models on an a100/h100 we can hit 200ms-ish with kv-cache warming and no big batch. with 30b we're 400-800ms depending on quantization.
[04:56] Raj: can you do mixed-precision or 4-bit quant? our memory is tight.
[05:02] Priya: yes we support quantized runtime profiles: 16-bit, 8-bit, and experimental 4/4-bit. we also support offloading KV cache to NVMe for longer sequences but that increases latency. for imaging workloads sequence length is smaller but embeddings sometimes large.

Hardware/footprint specifics:
[05:26] Maya: we need a reference footprint for a 13b model at target latency with 95th p99 SLO. what are the server recommendations?
[05:34] Priya: for 13b low-latency we'd typically recommend 1x H100 or 1x A100 80GB, with 256GB RAM and NVMe for cache; for 30b two GPU setups or higher-memory H100s. but given your rack/power constraints, we can provide a small-chassis config with external GPU chassis (egx enclosures) or a single 2U that holds one blade.
[05:57] Raj: our procurement might force us to keep TDP and physical size small. can Redwood support deployment to CPU fallback or hybrid with inference on CPU for non-latency-sensitive paths?
[06:07] Priya: yes we support CPU-only as a fallback but it'll be slower; we also support split routing so critical calls route to GPU and background batch calls to CPU or a cheaper instance.

Software update and change control:
[06:28] Samira: talk us through a typical offline update - from artifact build to install and verification.
[06:34] Priya: typical flow: we build the release artifact in a secure environment -> sign with our release key -> you receive a signed bundle (tar + manifest) via secure courier -> you upload to an isolated validation host -> run our offline installer which checks signatures against your truststore, validates digest, runs local unit tests (sanity checks), then pushes containers to the runtime host. we also support an air-gapped canary: you can test on a single node before rolling to the sterile cluster.
[07:06] Lina: for audits, we need to show who approved the change. does the installer record approver metadata?
[07:13] Priya: yes installer has a field for approver id and reason and generates an install log with timestamps and artifact digests. logs can be exported and fed into your SIEM.

Ops & rollback:
[07:32] Raj: what's rollback process if the new model regresses? can we pin models and quickly move back?
[07:38] Priya: you can pin model versions. our runtime supports immediate fallback to pinned model if health checks fail; the rollback is fast because model artifacts are cached locally. if you want stronger guarantees we advise keeping a golden copy on local NVMe to avoid re-fetching from sealed media.
[07:56] Maya: how big are these artifacts typically? 30b model image + runtime packaging?
[08:02] Priya: depends on quant, a 13b fp16 package might be ~20-30GB; 30b can be 60-90GB fp16. 4-bit quant reduces that dramatically, down to ~10-20GB. but remember runtime + libs add overhead.

Integration & networking:
[08:24] Samira: how do you plan to integrate with their PACS? do you need outgoing webhooks, etc?
[08:30] Dr. Evan Low: our pipeline uses DICOM rs/ qido stores; we can call local endpoints. the sterile room cannot do outbound webhooks, so everything is internal.
[08:40] Priya: we can expose a local REST/gRPC endpoint and a pull model that polls the queue, or operate as a sidecar within the pipeline. both work in isolated environments.

Billing and reserved capacity discussion:
[09:00] Samira: for enterprise we offer private license + support and optionally reserved capacity for non-air-gapped sites. since this is hermetic, billing is typically a license + support model. interested in commitments?
[09:11] Dr. Evan Low: we'll likely treat this as a capital procurement in the sterile site, but for other non-sensitive clusters we may want reserved capacity with Redwood.

Security deep-dive (Lina):
[09:24] Lina: question on keys: you said we can use local HSM. does Redwood ever retain any plaintext keys?
[09:30] Priya: no, we don't retain plaintext customer keys. we can ship artifacts signed by our release key and acceptance is based on your trust bundle. for customer-managed keys we do an encrypted key-wrap and we never see unwrapped keys.
[09:43] Lina: do you provide customer-facing pen test reports or red-team summaries?
[09:47] Samira: yes we have a security pack with SOC2 Type 2, ISO27001 summary, and infrastructure pentest summaries we can share under an NDA.

Failover and graceful degradation:
[10:05] Raj: what happens if GPU crashes mid-inference? do you have in-flight retry or sticky sessions?
[10:12] Priya: runtime maintains KV cache and we checkpoint client sessions; if a worker fails we attempt to replay from last checkpoint and fall back to a compatible model on a different worker. there may be a small latency spike but requests shouldn't error out if you enable automatic fallback.

Benchmarks & evaluation plan:
[10:32] Priya: propose we run a two-step POC: 1) an offsite synthetic benchmark using your sample DICOMs to pick optimal model/quant profile, 2) an on-site closed-lab run to validate latency with actual hardware and network isolation.
[10:48] Samira: timeline wise does late july for on-site bench work?
[10:52] Maya: yes procurement and facilities can probably provision a narrow window in late july. we'll confirm exact dates.

Questions from Quasar:
[11:05] Dr. Evan Low: will Redwood support GPU hotplug or live kernel upgrades? we prefer no reboots during shifts.
[11:13] Priya: we have mechanisms for live kernelless updates of the runtime components, but major OS kernel upgrades require scheduled maintenance. for runtime patching we support rolling updates at container level with sticky sessions drained first.
[11:29] Raj: is there a way to test upgrades locally without involving your release process? like can we build from source and run a local installer?
[11:37] Priya: yes we provide a developer offline kit for customers where you can produce your own signed artifacts if you maintain your own build chain. we'd want to validate compatibility but it supports that model.

[12:00] (discussion continues with back-and-forth; transcript abbreviated for brevity but this capture hits main points)

Recap and next steps:
[12:10] Samira: recap: 1) Samira sends security pack and SOW example, 2) Priya sends benchmark test plan, 3) Quasar supplies HW SKU list and confirms late-july window.
[12:25] Dr. Evan Low: correct, and we'll include manifest requirements for audit.
[12:30] Maya: i'll coordinate facilities and customs clearance for sealed media transfer.
[12:36] Samira: great, thanks all. we'll follow up in email with the artifacts.
[12:40] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: speakers occasionally overlap, some technical acronyms clipped (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed 'kay-vee cache' in places), proper nouns (model family names) may be slightly off in some auto text.
